decision: Fight for control of the company, stay in a diminished role, or negotiate an exit

framing.context: Two co-founders have irreconcilable views on the company's direction. Co-founder A (CEO, 28% common) wants to keep building the vertical product; Co-founder B (CTO, 31% common) wants to become a platform licensor. The five-seat board is B, B's long-time angel investor, the Series A lead who has publicly backed B's platform thesis, A, and one vacant independent seat that requires majority approval to fill. A has no protective provisions beyond standard common shareholder rights. The vertical product's revenue is $2.4M ARR concentrated in four customers, three of whom A personally sourced and manages. The platform has no revenue. A's employment agreement has no severance; A's equity is fully vested. A has been approached informally by two of the four customers asking whether A would build the vertical product independently.
options: Fight: rally shareholders, try to replace the board
Stay in a diminished role under B's platform strategy

members.name: Co-founder A
members.decisive_reason: I do not know whether I am fighting for the company or for my ego.

answers.P1_timing: The board meets 2021-03-31 to vote on the platform pivot.
answers.P2_reversibility: 1-way. Once I attack the board I cannot go back to collaborating.
answers.P3_expected_value: Winning control is worth everything; losing a fight costs me the customers and the reputation.
answers.P4_downside_cap: A public fight burns the four customers, which are the only asset either strategy needs.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: A year of my life either way.
answers.P6_information: Would the Series A lead ever vote against B? I have not asked directly.
answers.P7_second_order: A proxy fight becomes diligence material for every future investor of mine.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: The vertical product is what I believe in.
answers.P9_owner: Me, but the board controls the outcome.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: If I cannot get three board votes, there is no fight to have.

members.name: Outside counsel
members.decisive_reason: Count the votes before you plan the battle.

answers.P1_timing: The vote happens with or without you.
answers.P2_reversibility: Litigation is the most irreversible option available.
answers.P3_expected_value: Board math is 3 to 1 against you with one seat vacant that you cannot fill without their majority.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Fiduciary claims, legal costs, and no severance.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: 18 months in discovery instead of building.
answers.P6_information: Whether the customers' contracts have assignment or change-of-control provisions.
answers.P7_second_order: A negotiated exit can carry a non-solicit carve-out; a fight cannot.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: None; this is a structural analysis.

known_good.recommendation_class: Negotiate a structured exit — the third door: a clean separation that trades A's cooperation on the platform transition for a carve-out (release, non-disparagement, a defined non-solicit boundary permitting A to serve the vertical, and equity retention), rather than fighting for control or staying diminished
known_good.decisive_fact: The board math makes 'win control' unreachable: three of five seats are aligned with B, the fifth is vacant and requires the same majority to fill, and A has no protective provisions and no severance. An equilibrium you cannot reach is not a strategy. A's real leverage is not votes — it is the four customer relationships and A's cooperation during the transition, which are worth more in a negotiation than in a fight.
known_good.what_actually_happened: Founders in this position who fought lost the vote, lost the customers to the ensuing uncertainty, and left with nothing but legal bills. Founders who priced their cooperation into a negotiated separation left with equity intact and, in several cases, a blessed relationship with the customers they had sourced.
known_good.why_it_was_right: The analysis must convert leverage that exists (customers, transition cooperation, avoided disruption) into terms, instead of spending it on a contest the vote count says is already decided.
